profile.answer_block: Jin-Ho Lee is a data scientist with bioinformatics roots based in Mannheim, Germany. He spent eight years in academic research across bioinformatics and experimental biophysics with 12 peer-reviewed publications, and now ships production machine-learning and data pipelines, brings Google Cloud consulting experience from international banking, and has coached 100+ specialists in Python, SQL and ML. He holds an M.Sc. from Heidelberg University.
profile.tagline: Data scientist with bioinformatics roots — eight years of academic research, 12 peer-reviewed publications, production ML and cloud consulting on GCP; 1,000+ analytical processes migrated, 100+ specialists coached.
paragraphs: Worked across bioinformatics and experimental biophysics: unpublished NGS/RNA-Seq genomics project work (HLA typing and splice-derived neoepitope candidate pipelines) at the National Center for Tumor Diseases (NCT) and Seoul National University (SNU), plus quantitative bioimage analysis and wet-lab research at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Forschungszentrum Jülich (FZ Jülich), and Kirchhoff Institute for Physics (KIP). The experimental imaging / DNA-repair / chromatin / radiation-biology line produced 12 peer-reviewed research publications — first- and shared-first author — not genomics papers.

As a Cintellic consultant for an international bank, architected the migration of 1,000+ analytical processes to Google Cloud and shipped BigQueryML models for anti-financial-crime & KYC. Previously at neuefische, coached 100+ specialists in Python, SQL & ML; in research, secured third-party funding and supervised 10+ students.

D1.title: SignMeUp – Real-Time American Sign Language (ASL) Recognition
D1.summary: Built a real-time ASL recognition prototype: an end-to-end machine-learning pipeline that extracts hand landmarks, classifies temporal gestures, and gives sign-language learners immediate feedback.
contributions: Project Leadership: Defined project scope, managed team communication, and delivered stakeholder presentations.
Model Development: Designed and optimized an LSTM neural network to classify temporal sequences of ASL gestures.
Data Engineering: Developed a pipeline for real-time landmark extraction, feature engineering, and data cleaning from video feeds.
D1.outcome: Delivered a functional prototype for real-time inference, enabling instant feedback for sign language learners.

D2.title: badminton-vision – Real-Time On-Device Computer Vision for Badminton
D2.summary: Fully on-device Chrome MV3 extension for real-time badminton match analysis, with browser-based pose, racket, and shuttle detection; actively rebuilding toward its first stable release.
contributions: Built a Chrome MV3 extension that detects pose, racket, and shuttle on badminton match footage played on YouTube, running entirely client-side with no server round-trip.
Implemented the default real-time detection pipeline with TensorFlow.js and ONNX Runtime Web.
Evaluated an experimental zero-shot, open-vocabulary object detector (YOLO-World) alongside the default detector.
Applied full product-development discipline: a written PRD, UX wireframing and review, an automated test suite, and a CI pipeline.
Public on GitHub (Jin-HoMLee/badminton-vision); still in active development, not yet a finished v1.
D2.outcome: In-browser, on-device computer vision extension for badminton match analysis, under active, ongoing development toward a first stable release.

D3.summary: Coached multiple cohorts through an applied data-science program, combining Python, SQL, machine learning, visualization, and capstone delivery with hands-on technical mentoring.
contributions: Delivered lectures on Python, machine learning, SQL, and data visualization.
Mentored students throughout the data science lifecycle.
Supervised capstone projects and technical presentations.
Developed and improved training materials.
D3.outcome: Successfully supported multiple cohorts in developing industry-ready data science skills.

D4.title: claude-personas – Multi-Persona Framework for Claude Code
D4.summary: Framework for running multiple specialized Claude Code personas in parallel, each with its own isolated, role-specific persistent memory, so a solo developer can cover multiple roles across a project.
contributions: Designed a persona system (e.g. Developer, PM, Designer, Scientist) so one solo developer can run several specialized Claude Code agents in parallel instead of switching hats manually.
Built isolated, role-specific persistent memory per persona, so each agent accumulates and reuses its own context across sessions without polluting the others.
Set up a CI pipeline to keep the framework's own tooling and configuration reliable across changes.
Public on GitHub (Jin-HoMLee/claude-personas).
D4.outcome: An open-source framework that lets a solo developer parallelize multi-role work by running several specialized, memory-isolated Claude Code personas at once.

L1.title: Cancer Neoantigen Discovery – Transcriptome-Wide Splice Analysis
L1.summary: Unpublished computational pipeline predicting splice-junction–derived neoepitope candidate peptides from RNA-Seq data.
contributions: Developed a discovery pipeline to identify novel splice junctions in TCGA cancer cohorts (BRCA/LUAD/LAML RNA-seq).
Predicted HLA-A*02:01-binding candidate 9-mers from three-frame translation of short junction contigs.
Cross-referenced candidate junctions with published transcript/isoform reports.
Compared computational mutation-derived and splice-derived neoepitope candidate sets (no experimental co-targeting claim).
L1.outcome: SNU internship 2015: unpublished computational proof of concept — novel splice junctions in TCGA BRCA/LUAD/LAML RNA-seq, three-frame translation of short junction contigs, NetMHCpan predicted HLA-A*02:01 candidate 9-mers. No experimental validation, clinical use, publication, or patent.

L2.title: Personalized Immunotherapy – High-Throughput HLA Typing Pipeline
L2.summary: B.Sc. thesis project: Bioinformatics workflow for identifying patient-specific cancer targets and automating HLA genotyping from Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) data.
contributions: Developed an in silico genotyping pipeline to extract HLA alleles directly from Whole-Exome Sequencing (WXS) data.
Implemented predictive modeling using ANNs (NetMHCPan) to screen missense mutations for MHC-I binding affinity.
Engineered a consensus methodology integrating multiple HLA typing algorithms to resolve sequence ambiguities and improve call consistency.
Checked the pipeline computationally by comparing binding-specificity predictions across HLA alleles to flag inconsistent allele calls.
L2.outcome: B.Sc. thesis, NCT Heidelberg: in-silico HLA typing from WES/NGS and ANN-based MHC-I binding screens for missense-mutation candidates. Unpublished.

L3.title: Experimental Biophysics — Chromatin Nano-Architecture & DNA Repair
L3.summary: Advanced research utilizing super-resolution microscopy and computational analysis to investigate DNA repair mechanisms and chromatin nano-architecture.
contributions: Experimental Design: Developed and executed research projects focused on DNA repair pathways and super-resolution imaging of chromatin structures.
Data Analysis & Modeling: Leveraged MATLAB, R, and Python to process complex imaging data and perform quantitative analysis of nano-scale structures.
Academic Leadership: Managed international research collaborations and mentored several Bachelor and Master's students throughout the project lifecycle.
L3.outcome: Published research findings in multiple peer-reviewed journals and secured third-party funding for continued scientific investigations.

L4.title: Neural Stem Cell Research – Radiation Effects on 3D Differentiation
L4.summary: Scientific research project investigating the impact of ionizing radiation and extracellular vesicles on human neural progenitor cell differentiation.
contributions: Experimental Design: Developed and executed a multi-year research project at the intersection of radiation biology and neuroscience.
Leadership & Mentoring: Supervised and guided students, junior researchers, and technical staff through complex laboratory workflows.
Scientific Communication: Secured third-party funding, established research collaborations, and published findings in peer-reviewed journals.
L4.outcome: Successfully identified new insights into neural radiation responses and presented results at international scientific conferences.

L5.title: Splice Neoepitope Pipeline – Reproducible Snakemake Workflow
L5.summary: Modernised, open-source reimplementation of the 2015 SNU computational proof of concept for predicted splice-junction–derived neoepitope candidates as a reproducible Snakemake pipeline with optional structural modelling.
contributions: Re-engineered the original SNU pipeline as a fully reproducible Snakemake 8.x workflow with per-rule Conda environments — installable without manual dependency management; run locally and on GCP GPU VMs, and executor-portable to a SLURM cluster by design (per-rule resources + Conda) — a config swap, not a rewrite.

Implemented tumor-vs-matched-normal junction filtering against GENCODE annotation, assigning computational junction classes (annotated, normal_shared, tumor_exclusive) without experimental tumor-specificity proof.
Integrated patient-specific HLA typing (OptiType) and MHC-I peptide presentation prediction (MHCflurry 2.x Class1PresentationPredictor) for end-to-end neoepitope candidate ranking.
Added optional TCR-pMHC ternary complex structural modelling via TCRdock (AlphaFold v2 backend) on Google Cloud GPU; predicted complexes rendered as interactive Mol* 3D viewer in the report.
MIT-licensed, public on GitHub (Jin-HoMLee/splice-neoepitope-pipeline).
L5.outcome: Open-source Snakemake 8 workflow (MIT): RNA-Seq → junction classes vs matched normal + GENCODE → OptiType HLA → MHCflurry MHC-I candidate ranking; optional TCR-pMHC modelling. Ran locally and on GCP; SLURM-portable by design (not claimed as already run on SLURM). Modern reimplementation of the 2015 computational idea — new methods are 2026 work. Computational outputs only, not therapeutic claims.

faqs.question: Who is Jin-Ho Lee?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee combines cancer-genomics research with production data science and ML/AI engineering. He is based in Mannheim, Germany, and holds an M.Sc. in Molecular Biotechnology from Heidelberg University.

faqs.question: What is Jin-Ho Lee's professional background?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee spent eight years in doctoral and post-graduate research across Forschungszentrum Jülich, Kirchhoff Institute for Physics, National Center for Tumor Diseases, Seoul National University and the German Cancer Research Center, working on cancer genomics and super-resolution microscopy. He then moved to industry as a data science coach at neuefische and as a consultant and lead business functional analyst employed by Cintellic GmbH for an international bank; he now works independently on ML/AI engineering and open-source tooling.

faqs.question: What technical skills does Jin-Ho Lee have?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee works in Python, SQL and R, with machine learning in TensorFlow, bioinformatics pipelines in Snakemake, and cloud data engineering on Google Cloud including BigQuery and BigQueryML. His domain expertise spans cancer genomics, NGS and RNA-Seq analysis, HLA typing, neoantigen discovery, and spatial point-pattern analysis.

faqs.question: What has Jin-Ho Lee published?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee has 12 peer-reviewed research publications (10 articles and 2 research book chapters), including first-author and shared-first-author papers (2 first / 3 shared-first / 7 co-author), in radiation biophysics and super-resolution imaging of DNA-damage repair and chromatin architecture. The full list with citation counts is available via his ORCID record (0009-0001-8784-1771) and Google Scholar profile.

faqs.question: What is Jin-Ho Lee working on now?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee currently works independently on agentic AI systems - LLM agents with tool use, planning, routing, multi-agent orchestration and persistent memory - alongside open-source Claude Code tooling, a real-time, fully on-device computer-vision Chrome extension for badminton match analysis, and a reproducible Snakemake splice-neoepitope candidate pipeline with optional AlphaFold2 structural modelling.

faqs.question: Is Jin-Ho Lee available for new opportunities?
faqs.answer: Jin-Ho Lee's stated availability: open to roles in bioinformatics, computational biology and data science, based in Mannheim, Germany. The fastest way to reach him is the contact form on this site or the digital twin chat, which answers detailed questions about his experience and can pass on a message.
